reader.requirement: At --std 85, the comparisons ORD-MIN uses to find the least argument-1 are those of a 1985 simple (relation) condition: numeric operands by algebraic value regardless of usage, length of literals not significant and zero unique regardless of sign (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.1); nonnumeric operands character by character in the program collating sequence named in OBJECT-COMPUTER (native when none), the shorter extended on the right with spaces (§1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2). The witness covers algebraic order, collating order against length, and one padding tie; it does not exercise a non-native PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, usages other than DISPLAY, or signed zero.

reader.notes: The binder resolves an all-nonnumeric list (class-neutral figuratives do not vote) to OrdMinString and passes the PCS weights when a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE is in effect, so the function and an IF on the same operands agree (P8 vs P12). refuter.evidence: Attack aimed at the one carrier that could break algebraic comparison: CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#OrdMaxReal/OrdMinReal compare binary64 values. ordreal.cob at --std 85 mixes FUNCTION SQRT with 18-digit and 18-decimal-place items: N1 01, N2 02, N3 02, M3 02, matching IF B1 < B2 and IF F1 < F2, so the renderer lifts the approximate argument to decimal and the real body is not reached at 85. ordgrp.cob: group comparisons (G1/G2 with COMP subfields, H1/H2 signed DISPLAY in groups) agree with the IF relation on the same operands (GM 02 + REL G1<G2; HM 01 + REL H1>H2). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.33.4 RV2 'made according to the rules for simple conditions'.
